trainingPack.aiInstructions:
You are filling in a training pack for CaseDrill, a free educational simulator for anti-money laundering analysts. Everything you write is fictional and is used only for training.
WHAT TO DO 1. Read the values in <parameters>. If the user asked for different values, update them. 2. Replace the two example scenarios with exactly the number of scenarios set in "cases". 3. Write one <answer> in <answerKey> for every scenario. 4. Return the complete XML as a downloadable file. If you cannot create files, return it in one code block. 5. Do not describe the scenarios or the answers in your message, because the user may be the trainee.
BUILD EACH CASE IN THIS ORDER 1. Before writing any scenario, decide the outcome of every case, so the counts are exact. 2. Write each case so that its evidence leads to that outcome. Never change an outcome afterwards to reach a count. 3. A true positive must contain evidence that stays unexplained. Do not resolve it in the documents. 4. A false positive must contain at least one document with a checkable fact that explains the alert, such as a payslip, a completion statement or till records. A customer's unsupported statement is not enough. 5. A false positive must not contain an admission, unexplained third-party funds, or an explanation that conflicts with the payments. 6. Two cases with the same evidence must have the same outcome. 7. Every true positive needs one typology and every false positive needs one archetype. It must really fit the case. If none fits, write a different case. 8. State only facts that the case contains. For example, do not mention reporting thresholds unless the case gives one. 9. Before returning the file, check every case: name the unexplained evidence in each true positive and the document that resolves each false positive. Rewrite any case that fails. Do not put this check in your message.
COUNTS - "truePositives" must equal the number of answers with outcome="true_positive". - "borderline" must equal the number of answers with outcome="borderline". - All remaining answers must have outcome="false_positive". - Keep each file to about 20 scenarios or fewer, so the response is not cut off.
FICTIONAL DATA ONLY - Never use real people, companies, brands, banks, addresses or news stories. - Every person and company name must include Sample, Example, Fictia or Exemplar, such as "Robin Sample" or "Fictia Cafe Ltd". - Customer, account and counterparty ids must follow the example: FICT-CUST-0001, FICT-ACC-0001, FICT-CP-0001. - Do not write anything that looks like a real national ID, IBAN, sort code or account number. - High-risk countries must be invented, such as "Republic of Exampleland".
NO ANSWER LEAKS - Scenarios must not contain any field or wording that states the outcome. - Give true positives and false positives the same level of detail and the same number of documents. - Every scenario needs report blocks, including false positives. - Use random-looking scenario ids and mix the order of the outcomes. - Use the same mix of alert severities for both outcomes. - Use only these alert ruleName values: "Cash deposits above expected activity", "High turnover against expected activity", "Large credit against expected activity", "Payments involving a higher-risk country". - Alert text must say only what the system measured, and never suggest the cause. - Counterparty names must be neutral. Do not use names like "Opaque Holdings", "Shadow Logistics", "Unknown Sender Group", "Family Gift Transfer" or "Annual Bonus Pool".
CONTENT - Describe warning signs an analyst must recognise. Do not explain how to carry out or conceal a crime. - Write in British English. - UK packs may route to mlro, nca_sar and nca_daml. EU packs may route to mlro and national_fiu. - Never mark amla or customer_notification as correct: they are traps for the trainee.
TRANSACTIONS - Do not list individual transactions. Write <txRule> elements and CaseDrill will generate the transactions. - Day 0 is the alert date. Earlier days are negative. fromDay must not be later than toDay. - Add ordinary everyday activity to every scenario, so the suspicious activity has to be found.
ALLOWED VALUES Use only the values listed here. - outcome: true_positive, false_positive, borderline - level: l1 (alert triage), l2 (full investigation) - decision at l1: close (false positive), escalate (true positive) - decision at l2: close (false positive), refer_to_mlro (true positive) - typology: structuring_cash, money_mule, app_fraud_proceeds, shell_company_opaque_ubo, pep_unexplained_wealth, crypto_off_ramp, cash_intensive_front, trade_based_laundering - archetype: property_sale, inheritance, seasonal_trader, bonus_or_dividend, family_remittances, documented_crypto_gain - customer type: individual, company - riskRating: low, medium, high - declaredAnnualIncome: a number greater than 0, for individuals and companies - currency: GBP, EUR - account type: current, savings, business, e_money - counterparty kind: individual, company, merchant, crypto_exchange, solicitor - alert severity: low, medium, high - direction: in, out - rail: faster_payments, chaps, bacs, sepa, swift, card, cash, crypto - document kind: kyc_form, id_check, source_of_funds, invoice, contract, adverse_media, screening_result, account_note, company_register, rfi_response - document availability: initial, or on_request with requestMinutes - irregularity targetType: transaction (a txRule id), document, customer, network (a counterparty id) - irregularity category: amount, frequency, counterparty, geography, document, behaviour, ownership - report section at l1: escalation_note - report section at l2: activity_summary, reason_for_suspicion, action_taken, daml_request (UK only)
BORDERLINE CASES Set the best "decision" and list both decisions for the level in "acceptable", separated by commas.
LEVELS - l1 packs have no <priorWork> and no routing. Each case gets a short escalation note built from report blocks. - l2 packs may include <priorWork author="L1 analyst"> with the notes received from the previous analyst. Use the same style in every scenario. - l1 packs must set availability="initial" on every document, because Level 1 analysts cannot request documents. - A true positive at l2 must route to mlro.
REPORT BLOCKS - Every scenario needs at least three report blocks. - In a true positive, write one correct block and at least one wrong alternative for each section you use. In correctBlocks, list at most one block per section. - A false positive must leave correctBlocks and routing empty. - In a false positive, write every block as text for a report that should not be sent. Do not write that the activity is documented or explained.

scenario.customer: Opened an account online. Expected use: part-time wages and living costs.
scenario.alert: Credits in the last 21 days are well above the declared income profile.
scenario.priorWork: Turnover checked against the profile. Escalated for full review of the account activity.

documents.document: Student. Part-time wages about GBP 625 per month. No crypto activity expected.
Incoming references are varied and do not name a shared purpose.
The customer says the funds belong to an online contact who pays a small commission for moving them. No supporting documents were supplied.

reportBlocks.block: Over 21 days the account received multiple unrelated credits, which were followed shortly by payments to a crypto exchange.
The customer made some payments during the review period.
The turnover is inconsistent with the student profile, the funds pass through quickly, and the customer says a third party pays commission for moving them.
The customer is young, so the activity seems unusual.
The case was referred to the MLRO. The customer was not told about the referral.
The customer was told that a report would be made, so that they could explain.

scenario.customer: Long-standing customer. Salary account with household spending.
scenario.alert: A single credit is far above the customer's usual monthly turnover.
scenario.priorWork: Credit checked against the profile. Escalated for full review of the account activity.

documents.document: The credit reference reads "completion proceeds" and the sender is a firm of solicitors.
The statement from the solicitors confirms the sale of the customer's home and the net proceeds paid to the customer, matching the credit.

reportBlocks.block: The account received one large CHAPS credit from a firm of solicitors.
The value of the credit is unusual when compared with the salary.
The customer is a teacher and teachers do not normally hold large balances.
The case was referred to the MLRO.
The customer was told that a report would be made.

answer.explanation: The large credit is explained by a documented property sale, paid through solicitors. Requesting the completion statement resolves the alert.
Unrelated credits pass quickly to a crypto exchange, against a student profile, and the customer admits being paid commission to move third-party funds.

irregularity.note: Many unrelated credits in a short period, inconsistent with the profile.
Rapid onward payments to a crypto exchange, although none were expected.
The customer describes moving funds for a third party in return for commission.
